description: The hand-verified expected result for the DERIVED Semgrep SARIF fixture. This is not a captured artifact and is not held to AAP 0.6.2's unmodified-excerpt requirement: it is a derived fixture whose whole purpose is to carry the SARIF feature cases no captured artifact in this provisioning contains, so that moving oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/semgrep.sarif to a true capture drops no coverage. Every value below was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match.

provenance.derived_from: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/semgrep.sarif as that file stood before it was rebuilt as a true captured excerpt of harness/artifacts/raw/semgrep.sarif. This file carries those exact bytes, so the coverage that fixture provided is retained rather than deleted; the sha256 and byte size above are that earlier file's, which is why they are identical to the ones the pre-rebuild semgrep expectation recorded.
provenance.ultimate_source: harness/artifacts/raw/semgrep.sarif for the rule objects and the message texts, which are the producer's own; everything named under authored_feature_cases and alterations below is not.
authored_feature_cases: a run.originalUriBaseIds base map -- %SRCROOT% resolving to file:///opt/spark-src/ -- so that the SARIF 2.1.0 section 3.4.4 walk completes and the sarif-uri-base-id-chain path basis is exercised. No captured SARIF artifact in this provisioning emits originalUriBaseIds at all: measured over all three raw artifacts, the member is absent from every run.

a result carrying a ruleIndex and no ruleId, at a non-zero index, so the indexed rule-resolution route and the rule_id_from_rule_index counter are exercised. No opengrep or semgrep result carries a ruleIndex, and every datadog-static-analyzer result carries both ruleId and ruleIndex with ruleId outranking it, so no captured excerpt can move that counter.

a rule listing three CVE identifiers out of ascending order, so the ascending-numeric CVE rule and the multi_valued_cve_records counter are exercised. No rule in any of the three raw SARIF artifacts carries more than one distinct CVE identifier: measured over 2002, 2126 and 1093 rules.
a result carrying no uriBaseId at all alongside five that carry one, so both the sarif-uri-base-id-chain and sarif-no-uri-base-id-metadata-base path bases appear in one document.

four results stating a level of their own alongside two that do not, so the result-borne level source and the rule defaultConfiguration derivation are both exercised in one document; every captured semgrep and opengrep result omits level.
alterations: runs[0].originalUriBaseIds is authored: the raw artifact carries no such member.

The six results are authored. Measured over the raw artifact's 1162 results, none carries a level, none carries a ruleIndex, none omits ruleId, none omits uriBaseId on its first location, and the run emits no originalUriBaseIds at all.

Driver rules 0 to 4 are the raw artifact's own rule objects with their help and helpUri members removed -- every remaining member is byte-equal to the raw rule carrying the same id -- and rule 5 states in its own fullDescription that it was authored for these tests.
runs[0].invocations carries executionSuccessful and no toolExecutionNotifications, where the raw artifact's invocation carries 179 of them.
provenance.not_altered: Every authored location is anchored to a real construct at the pinned commit -- DiskStore.scala line 76 is the logDebug interpolation and lines 83 to 85 the shuffleServiceFetchRddEnabled block, OneForOneBlockPusher.java lines 85 to 86 the BlockPushReturnCode decode, and test_evaluation.py lines 59, 157 and 337 the three tempfile.TemporaryDirectory statements -- so no row below cites a line the pinned tree does not carry.
provenance.must_never_be_read_as_captured: test_sarif_adapter.py, RawArtifactProvenanceTests.test_every_derived_fixture_is_declared_derived_and_is_not_a_raw_excerpt asserts both halves of this: that this expectation declares the fixture derived, and that its results are NOT all present in the raw artifact -- so this file can never be mistaken for a capture, in either direction.

fixture.excerpt_note: Not an excerpt. See provenance above.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

resolution_context.root_independence: Not root-independent, unlike the three captured fixtures, and that is a property of this artifact rather than a defect in it. This run's originalUriBaseIds names an absolute base, file:///opt/spark-src/, so the five results carrying a uriBaseId resolve to their uri unchanged precisely because that base is the recorded scan root; joined onto any other root the same references would relativize with ../ segments and take path_kind outside_root. The rows below therefore hold for the scan root named under scan_root, and no absolute path appears anywhere in this file.
resolution_context.scan_root_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the semgrep entry's resolved_scan_root, which is the value of SPARK_SRC -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the semgrep entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.sarif_uri_base_id_observed: %SRCROOT% on five of the six results; the sixth carries no uriBaseId at all
resolution_context.uri_base_id_walk_consequence: The base map carries one entry and that entry carries no uriBaseId of its own, so the SARIF 2.1.0 section 3.4.4 walk terminates at depth 1 on the absolute file:///opt/spark-src/ and completes. This is the single-level unchained case, and completing the walk is what keeps the metadata-backed fallback off the live path here: nothing in this fixture exercises a chained base, a cycle, an over-depth chain, a missing base entry or a degenerate base.
resolution_context.path_basis: sarif-uri-base-id-chain on the five results carrying a uriBaseId, and sarif-no-uri-base-id-metadata-base on the one that does not; the per-row value is in row_derivations
resolution_context.severity_source: Four of the six results state a level of their own. The two that do not take the level their rule states under defaultConfiguration.level, which is SARIF 2.1.0's own derivation for a result that omits the property rather than an inference about it. No rule here carries properties.severity or properties.problem.severity, so every severity_native is a SARIF level literal and every severity_norm comes from the level table: error High, warning Medium, note Low, none Info.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A SARIF result names a code location rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of runs[].results[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): twenty authored keys, one path_kind_* per path kind and one severity_basis_* per severity basis.
counters_note: Of the four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool, three are 0 for this fixture and one is not. Every result carries exactly one location, no rule carries more than one CWE identifier, and every path names a file inside the scanned tree, so multi_location_records, multi_valued_cwe_records and non_filesystem_paths are all 0. multi_valued_cve_records is 1: the record at /runs/0/results/4, whose rule lists three CVE identifiers. rule_id_from_rule_index is 1 for the same reason the fixture exists -- one result carries a ruleIndex and no ruleId -- and severity_from_rule_default_configuration is 2 because two results state no level of their own.

corroboration.agreement: not-applicable -- no dataset row corresponds to an authored result
corroboration.note: Row-for-row corroboration is not available here, and recording that is more useful than a number shaped like one: none of this fixture's six path and start_line pairs appears among the committed dataset's 1162 semgrep rows, because the results are authored rather than captured. What the dataset does corroborate is the rule-level mapping these rows assert. Its one semgrep row for opt.blitzy-harness.rules.semgrep-rules.scala.lang.security.audit.tainted-sql-string, at core/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/storage/DiskStore.scala line 72, carries severity_native error, severity_norm High and cwe CWE-89 -- the three values row 0 below derives for that same rule from that same rule metadata. That is corroboration recorded after the fact, not the source of these values.

rows.message: User data flows into this manually-constructed SQL string. User data can be safely inserted into SQL strings using prepared statements or an object-relational mapper (ORM). Manually-constructed SQL strings is a possible indicator of SQL injection, which could let an attacker steal or manipulate data from the database. Instead, use prepared statements (`connection.PreparedStatement`) or a safe library.

Found object deserialization using ObjectInputStream. Deserializing entire Java objects is dangerous because malicious actors can create Java object streams with unintended consequences. Ensure that the objects being deserialized are not user-controlled. If this must be done, consider using HMACs to sign the data stream to make sure it is not tampered with, or consider only transmitting object fields and populating a new object.
